results.description: SCAFFOLD consistently outperforms FEDAVG in terms of MSE across all numbers of clients N ∈ {10, 100, 1000, 10000} and both linear and logistic regression.
results.evidence:
results/formal/figure1/summary.csv, final communication round (50) mean_mse values:
LINEAR: N=10: SCAFFOLD=104.20 vs FEDAVG=175.99; N=100: SCAFFOLD=2.83 vs FEDAVG=5.03; N=1000: SCAFFOLD=0.611 vs FEDAVG=1.353; N=10000: SCAFFOLD=0.054 vs FEDAVG=0.135.
LOGISTIC: N=10: SCAFFOLD=0.01793 vs FEDAVG=0.2673; N=100: SCAFFOLD=0.000597 vs FEDAVG=0.06165; N=1000: SCAFFOLD=0.000163 vs FEDAVG=0.02276; N=10000: SCAFFOLD=0.000134 vs FEDAVG=0.01413.
SCAFFOLD strictly outperforms FEDAVG (lower MSE) in all 8 cases (4 N values × 2 problem types).
results.note: Final MSE taken at round 50 (the last recorded round) for each configuration. All comparisons are consistent across all seeds (3 seeds per config, mean reported).

results.description: In linear regression, as the number of clients increases, the stationary MSE of SCAFFOLD decreases, with N=10000 achieving lower error than N=1000, N=1000 lower than N=100, and N=100 lower than N=10.
results.evidence: File: results/formal/figure1/summary.csv — SCAFFOLD final MSE (communication_round=50) on linear regression: N=10: 104.199, N=100: 2.827, N=1000: 0.611, N=10000: 0.054. All three required ordering constraints hold: 0.054 < 0.611 < 2.827 < 104.199 (lower is better).
results.note: Stationary MSE taken as the value at the last recorded round (round 50) for each N. The monotone decrease with increasing N is clear and unambiguous across all four client counts.

results.description: In logistic regression, as the number of clients increases from 10 to 1000, the stationary MSE of SCAFFOLD decreases, with N=1000 lower than N=100 and N=100 lower than N=10.
results.evidence: results/formal/figure1/summary.csv, logistic/scaffold, round 50 (stationary): N=10 MSE=0.017931, N=100 MSE=0.000597, N=1000 MSE=0.000163. Ordering: N=1000 (0.000163) < N=100 (0.000597) < N=10 (0.017931) — both constraints SCAFFOLD(N=1000) > SCAFFOLD(N=100) and SCAFFOLD(N=100) > SCAFFOLD(N=10) are satisfied under lower_is_better.
results.note: The avg of last 5 rounds tells the same story: N=10=0.02166, N=100=0.000561, N=1000=0.000164, confirming monotone decrease in stationary MSE as N increases.

results.description: In logistic regression, there is no improvement in stationary MSE from N=1000 to N=10000.
results.evidence: From results/formal/figure1/plot_data/logistic_N1000_scaffold.csv and logistic_N10000_scaffold.csv (confirmed by summary.csv): SCAFFOLD logistic regression stationary MSE (average of last 10 rounds across 3 seeds) is ~1.570e-4 for N=1000 and ~1.270e-4 for N=10000. summary.csv last-round mean_mse: N=1000 = 1.630e-4, N=10000 = 1.342e-4. The predicate stationary_mse(N=10000) >= stationary_mse(N=1000) is FALSE: N=10000 achieves a clearly lower MSE (~19% lower), meaning there IS improvement from N=1000 to N=10000 in logistic regression, contradicting the claim.
results.note: The claim states no improvement from N=1000 to N=10000 in logistic regression (SCAFFOLD), but both the per-seed CSV files and the aggregate summary.csv show N=10000 consistently achieves lower stationary MSE (~1.27–1.34e-4) compared to N=1000 (~1.57–1.63e-4). This is counter to the paper's claim about logistic regression showing no linear speedup in the stationary regime.
